source_refs.note: Exercise 11.3, Question 7: carnival wheel, diameter 40 ft, centre 28 ft, 120 s per turn; three unlabelled asks, labelled (a)-(c) as in the answer key PDF 309.

blocks.prompt: 7 (a) [not labelled in print; the answer key calls it (a)] A carnival ride consists of a vertical wheel with a diameter of 40 feet. The centre of the wheel is 28 feet above the ground. The wheel rotates at a constant speed and takes 120 seconds to make one complete revolution. Model an equation that describes the height \(h(t)\) of a rider on the wheel as a function of time \(t\).
blocks.explanation:
Same kind of model as Question 5, but now the centre height is given directly.
Plan: radius \(=\) half the diameter; \(c = \frac{2\pi}{120}\); start at the bottom.
steps:
Given: diameter 40 ft, centre 28 ft above the ground, one revolution in 120 s.
To find: a formula for \(h(t)\).
Method: \(h = \text{centre} - \text{radius} \times \cos(ct)\), taking \(t = 0\) when the rider is at the lowest point (the question does not say; the key uses this start).

Radius (amplitude)
\[r = \tfrac{40}{2} = 20 \text{ ft}\]
Why: Half the diameter.

Centre (midline)
\[a = 28 \text{ ft}\]
Why: Given directly. Lowest point \(28 - 20 = 8\) ft, highest \(28 + 20 = 48\) ft.

Angular speed
\[c = \dfrac{2\pi}{120} = \dfrac{\pi}{60}\]
Why: One turn (\(2\pi\)) takes 120 s.

Write the model
\[h(t) = 28 - 20\cos\left(\tfrac{\pi}{60}t\right)\]
Why: \(-\cos\) starts at its lowest value, so \(h(0) = 8\) ft, the bottom of the wheel.

Check
\[h(0) = 8,\; h(60) = 48,\; h(120) = 8 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Bottom, top after half a turn, bottom again after a full turn.

answer_figure.alt: Graph of h(t) = 28 minus 20 cos(pi t over 60) for t from 0 to 120 seconds. The curve starts at (0, 8), peaks at (60, 48) and passes (90, 28) on the centre line. A horizontal line h = 36 cuts the curve at t about 37.86 s and t about 82.14 s.
answer_figure.caption: Exercise 11.3 Q7: rider height over one revolution, with the 36 ft line (plotted from the model; original drawing)

blocks.prompt: 7 (b) [not labelled in print] A carnival ride consists of a vertical wheel with a diameter of 40 feet. The centre of the wheel is 28 feet above the ground. The wheel rotates at a constant speed and takes 120 seconds to make one complete revolution. How high is the rider from the ground after 90 seconds?
blocks.explanation:
Substitution: put \(t = 90\) in the model.
Plan: angle \(\frac{90\pi}{60} = \frac{3\pi}{2}\), whose cosine is 0.
steps:
Given: \(h(t) = 28 - 20\cos\left(\tfrac{\pi}{60}t\right)\), \(t = 90\).
To find: \(h(90)\).
Method: Substitute and use \(\cos\frac{3\pi}{2} = 0\).

Check
Why: 90 s is three-quarters of a turn: the rider has passed the top (60 s) and is level with the centre on the way down, which is 28 ft.

blocks.prompt: 7 (c) [not labelled in print] A carnival ride consists of a vertical wheel with a diameter of 40 feet. The centre of the wheel is 28 feet above the ground. The wheel rotates at a constant speed and takes 120 seconds to make one complete revolution. At what times will the rider be 36 feet above the ground?
blocks.explanation:
Solve \(h(t) = 36\); in one turn there are two answers (going up and coming down).
Plan: isolate the cosine, find both angles in \([0, 2\pi)\), convert to times.
steps:
Given: \(h(t) = 28 - 20\cos\left(\tfrac{\pi}{60}t\right)\), \(h = 36\).
To find: all \(t\) with \(h(t) = 36\).
Method: Isolate \(\cos\); cosine is negative in Quadrants II and III, giving two angles per turn.

Get the cosine alone
\[28 - 20\cos\left(\tfrac{\pi}{60}t\right) = 36\]
\[-20\cos\left(\tfrac{\pi}{60}t\right) = 8\]
\[\cos\left(\tfrac{\pi}{60}t\right) = -0.4\]
Why: Subtract 28, divide by \(-20\).

Both angles in one turn
\[\cos^{-1}(0.4) = 66.42^{\circ}\]
\[\tfrac{\pi}{60}t = 113.58^{\circ} \text{ or } 246.42^{\circ}\]
Why: Reference angle \(66.42^{\circ}\); Quadrant II: \(180^{\circ} - 66.42^{\circ}\); Quadrant III: \(180^{\circ} + 66.42^{\circ}\).

Change to times
\[\tfrac{\pi}{60}t = 3t \text{ degrees}\]
\[t_1 = \tfrac{113.58}{3} \approx 37.86 \text{ s}\]
\[t_2 = \tfrac{246.42}{3} \approx 82.14 \text{ s}\]
Why: \(\frac{\pi}{60}\) rad \(= 3^{\circ}\), so the angle in degrees is \(3t\).

Check
\[t_1 + t_2 = 120 \;\checkmark\]
\[28 - 20\cos(113.58^{\circ}) = 28 + 8 = 36 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The two times are symmetric about the top (60 s). The key's 37.87 s and 82.13 s come from rounding the angle to \(113.6^{\circ}\); the same answer to one decimal place. The pattern repeats every 120 s.
blocks.final_answer: \(t \approx 37.86\) s and \(t \approx 82.14\) s (then every 120 s later)
